To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the crystal structure of the Sulfolobous solfataricus Swi2/Snf2 ATPase core bound to dsDNA reveals a novel DNA binding mode that is consistent with the mechanism of action of Swi2/Snfs in chromatin remodeling.
the SWI2/SWF2 ATPase core is a DNA translocase, and the structural switch that couples DNA binding to ATPase activation is a key element of the SWI2-SWF2 ATPase mechanism.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and function of the SWI2/SWF2 family of ATP-dependent chromatin remodeling complexes.
the molecular mechanism of DNA translocation and ATP-driven torque generation by SWI2/SWF2 ATPases.
the molecular mechanisms of DNA translocation and superhelix generation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SWI2/SWF2 ATPases are a family of ATP-dependent DNA translocases.
the structures of the SWI2/SWF2 ATPase core reveal two helical specific SWI2/SW2F2 subdomains, fused into a DExx motif related ATPase core.
the SWI2/Snf2 ATPase core of Sulfolobus solfatarius is a helicase-like ATPase that binds dsDNA in a non-separating manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have determined the first crystal structures of a SWI2/SWF2 ATPase core.
SWI2-SNF2 ATPases are a novel family of DNA translocases that move along the minor groove of duplex DNA without strand separation.
the SWI2/SWF2 ATPase core has two distinct DNA-binding sites, one for DNA translocation and another for ATP hydrolysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SWI2-SNF2 ATPases translocate along dsDNA, not ssDNA, and that they generate torque by a screw motion of dsDNA along a central c left.
SWI/SNF remodelers are not helicases, and that the ATPase domain does not directly contact the dsDNA.
SWI2/ SNF2 proteins use a DNA minor-groove translocation mechanism to unwind and remodel DNA.
